title: vault-dictionary — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_dictionary_blob_raw + protocol::decode_dictionary_blob — the MYD1 vault.dictionary encrypted personal-dictionary codec (MYND-266; §9.13). vault.dictionary is a vault-level singleton blob sealed under personal_dictionary_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::PersonalDictKey), with account_number_hash bound via aad_personal_dictionary_blob. The inner plaintext is OPAQUE bytes (the desktop layer's serialized {personal_words, ignore_words} word sets) — unlike vault-prefs there is no canonical-JSON inner shape; the structural twin of vault-search / vault-workspace / vault-indices. The HKDF role 'personal-dictionary-key' is DISTINCT from the AAD role 'personal-dictionary-blob' (different load-bearing strings). Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per DictionaryBlobError decode variant). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/dictionary_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.13 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-dictionary/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives personal_dictionary_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::PersonalDictKey, role string 'personal-dictionary-key') before calling the encoder.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 53-byte AAD via aad_personal_dictionary_blob (role string 'personal-dictionary-blob' — DISTINCT from the HKDF role 'personal-dictionary-key').

input_plaintext_hex.description: Opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), variable length including zero (empty = the empty dictionary). The codec treats these bytes as client-opaque (the desktop layer's serialized word sets); there is no canonical-JSON discipline here, unlike vault-prefs.

input_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_personal_dictionary_key_he.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::PersonalDictKey). Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_vault_dictionary_blob_hex assertion; carried so reviewers don't have to re-derive to inspect intermediate state.

expected_vault_dictionary_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: Recovered opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), empty allowed. The decoder returns these for the desktop layer to deserialize.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: DictionaryBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault (wrong account_number_hash) vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects (bad magic, unsupported dict_format_version, etc.) are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / dict_format_version / length checks all run before the AEAD stage (spec §9.13.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: DictionaryBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, DictFormatUnsupported, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated, CiphertextLenOverflow}). NOTE the dictionary codec names its format-version variant DictFormatUnsupported, but the vector string stays 'format_unsupported' for cross-family consistency. Unlike the AEAD failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are pre-decryption and intentionally distinguishable: a port must reject e.g. a future dict_format_version cleanly so the caller can fall back to the empty dictionary (§9.13.4).
